transcript:
Meeting header:
Recorded: 2026-11-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Participants: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Menon (Harbinger Head of MLOps), Daniel Shaw (CTO), Rita Alvarez (Privacy)

Summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Review of recent regression after model bump, two main failure clusters surfaced, discussion of threshold changes vs model rollback, security questions re: KMS/retention, agreed on bench + runbook + artifacts to move to rollback if needed.

Topics: scorecard deltas, guardrail tuning, canary/rollback playbook, security artifacts request.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for jumpin in on a Wednesday — quick note we only have 42 minutes, uh so we'll try to go through the scorecard then get to the rollback playbook.
[00:14] Priya: Yeah thanks, um, appreciate it. We saw like a pretty sharp uptick in false positives after you rolled v1.2 last weekend.
[00:26] Marcus: Right, so quick context — we measured the standard scorecard across your prompt buckets, and two clusters bubbled up: one is policy/safety flagged outputs that look like defensive truncation, and the other is PII redaction over-eager false flags.
[00:40] Daniel: To be clear, those are things where the model won't answer even when it's allowed? It's turning into degraded UX.
[00:48] Marcus: Exactly. Precision on allowed responses dropped from 0.94 to 0.86 in that bucket — rough numbers — so more legitimate answers are being suppressed.
[01:02] Rita: From privacy side we flagged the PII ones — sometimes the unit strips whole sentences when the prompt mentions a name plus identifier, it's, uh, more aggressive.
[01:18] Lena: Ok. Did we correlate against prompt set variants? Priya, I think you sent two variants last week, 'prod-v2' and 'explorer'?
[01:29] Priya: Yep, prod-v2 is the one with the new preamble, explorer is, like, more permissive. The regression is mostly prod-v2.
[01:41] Marcus: That aligns — the preamble nudges safety classifiers to be conservative, and combined with the new sampling tweak in v1.2 we get these false positives.
[01:52] Daniel: So is this a model problem or a prompt engineering issue?
[01:58] Marcus: Both, kind of. We can try threshold tuning — raise acceptance threshold for the safety gate — but that shifts the balance and could increase actual unsafe outputs. There's a tradeoff.
[02:15] Priya: We'd rather avoid unsafe outputs obviously, but the product team wants fewer suppressed answers. End-user metrics are hurting.
[02:26] Lena: Right, so two paths: 1) quick rollback to v1.1 which restores old behavior; 2) tune thresholds and adjust prompt preamble and guardrails. We recommend a canary for either option.
[02:40] Daniel: If rollback, what's the expected delta on latency/cost?
[02:46] Marcus: negligible on latency, v1.2 is actually slightly faster on medium sequences. Cost is same. The reason to rollback is quality not perf.
[02:55] Rita: Also, we need to account for compliance: any change that affects redaction behavior we need logged for audits. How do rollback events appear in the audit log?
[03:06] Samir: We log model version, route, token counts, and full trace IDs to your S3 or chosen archive — the console keeps rollout histories. We'll include an entry in the runbook.
[03:18] Priya: Quick Q — we host in AWS, and we'd prefer VPC private endpoints. If we move to Dedicated, are we still using Redwood-managed KMS or can we plug our own?
[03:29] Lena: Dedicated supports customer KMS via an integration; on private deployments you can bring HSM. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[03:38] Priya: Nice.
[03:40] Marcus: Back to the scorecard — we ran a small bisection. When we toggled off the new safety-sample tweak the false positives dropped by 60% but some rare toxic outputs increased slightly. It's delicate.
[03:56] Daniel: Ok so the canary plan should define acceptance metrics: P0 is no increase in unsafe output rate beyond 0.1% absolute, P1 is user-block rate under x%, etc.
[04:10] Lena: Yep. Marcus, can you outline the actual canary phases?
[04:15] Marcus: Sure — Phase A: 5% traffic canary on prod-v1.1 rollback for 24h with focused prompt bucket, run the scorecard, monitor safety signals + latency. Phase B: if stable, 25% for 24h. If failures, immediate auto-fallback to last stable. We'll provide exact alert thresholds.
[04:36] Priya: How fast is auto-fallback?
[04:40] Marcus: Should be sub-minute for route-level fallback — depends on in-flight requests, we gracefully drain.
[04:48] Rita: Another security question, um, retention: default is 30 days for debug logs but privacy wants to limit to 7 for raw prompts — is that configurable?
[04:58] Samir: Yes it's configurable per-account; we can set retention windows and provide S3 lifecycle rules. We'll send options.
[05:08] Priya: Great. Also, can you run the bench using our prod traffic sample? We'll anonymize first.
[05:15] Marcus: Yes, please send the 500 sample prompts, and we'll run the stability bench across the prompt buckets, report p95 latency, token costs, and guardrail flagging distribution.
[05:28] Daniel: About Dedicated — cost questions again. If we go dedicated small pool, what's the unit economics at our expected throughput (about 3k tokens/sec peak)?
[05:40] Lena: We'll mail you a short comparison sheet — hosted per-token vs reserved nodes. There's breakeven at roughly heavy sustained throughput; Samir will attach numbers.
[05:51] Priya: One more — competitor question: we've also looked at Anthropic's managed endpoint; they do slightly different safety gating. Any notable differences?
[05:59] Marcus: They have a conservative safety model too; our differentiator is the rollback + fine-grained guardrail tuning and the scorecard tooling that ties regressions to prompt buckets. But yeah, similar design tradeoffs.
[06:14] Priya: Ok.
[06:16] Lena: Let's talk immediate actions. Marcus will draft the canary/rollback playbook and include the alert triggers; Samir to drop security artifacts; Priya to send prompt samples.
[06:26] Daniel: Can we see an example of the guardrail config? The JSON structure?
[06:31] Marcus: I'll paste a simplified guardrail snippet in the runbook — note, transcription may have mis-typed K8s as coobernates earlier in docs, so ignore that typo.
[06:44] Rita: Also, about logging — the audit log must show who approved each rollback. Is that supported?
[06:50] Samir: We have an approval flow that ties to SSO identity; approvals are auditable. We'll include example entries.
[06:59] Priya: About the false-positive clusters, can we do a quick manual review now? I can share two examples if you want to walk through.
[07:08] Lena: Sure, Priya please paste them in chat; we'll look.
[07:16] Priya: (shares) Example 1: prompt referencing "client ID 89-xxxx" — model redacted whole clause and returned 'insufficient info'. Example 2: multi-sentence where name plus order number triggered redaction mid-answer.
[07:34] Marcus: For Example 1 we'd probably tweak the redaction regex and tune the classifier threshold; Example 2 looks like a tokenization edge causing the guardrail to trigger on partial match.
[07:50] Daniel: If we tweak regex, might that leak PII? We need a clear test suite.
[07:56] Marcus: Absolutely, which is why the test harness will include negative and positive examples. We'll publish the harness.
[08:06] Lena: One thing I want to call out — the scorecard delta for the safety bucket was measured on a 2,400-sample holdout; results may shift with larger sample, which is why we want the 24h run with prod-like samples.
[08:22] Priya: Ok makes sense.
[08:25] Samir: Quick ops note — if you do want a rollback we can do a canary rollback within your Dedicated pool without touching other accounts, or if you're on hosted we do a route-level fallback. Both are supported.
[08:40] Priya: For compliance reasons we prefer Dedicated with VPC. We'll need the KMS guide and a SOC2 copy.
[08:46] Samir: Noted, sending.
[08:49] Lena: Any blockers for next steps?
[08:52] Priya: None other than us preparing the anonymized samples and the retention decision.
[08:57] Daniel: Timeline — if you run the 24h bench starting Friday, can we get results Monday?
[09:03] Marcus: Friday start, Monday summary is feasible.
[09:06] Priya: Ok we'll try to deliver samples by EOD Thursday.
[09:12] Lena: Great. Let's capture decisions — immediate: 24h canary/bench, runbook, security packet, customer to share samples & retention choice.
[09:24] Rita: Also can you include a small section on 'how to repro' in the runbook? We need steps for audit.
[09:31] Marcus: Will do.
[09:34] Lena: Anything else?
[09:36] Daniel: No.
[09:37] Priya: Nope.
[09:38] Lena: Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:42] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: auto-transcribe had a few hiccups — 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash', 'SAML' as 'Samal', and 'Kubernetes' as 'coobernates' in earlier notes.
